comment: The xfail registry: cells that are KNOWN broken. A registry, not a deletion —
a cell listed here is reported as `xfail` when it fails and, crucially, as
`xpass` (which FAILS the run) when it starts passing. That forces the entry
to be removed when a fix lands, instead of the fix quietly going unnoticed.
Nothing may be silently absent from the matrix. A cell is either covered,
explicitly skipped with a typed reason, or listed here.

xfail.summary: a uint64 above int64max degrades to double INSIDE a container

measured.echoUint(2^64-1): 18446744073709551615 on both — a top-level scalar is exact

note: The C++ provider LOOKS green for [uint] only because its typed decode
coerces the double back to uint64_t; the Rust provider takes the value
untyped (serde_json::Value) and so reports the loss faithfully. Same
defect, one surface masking it.
logos-protocol's own bridge (logos_json_convert.cpp) handles unsigned
correctly and documents this hazard, so the loss is downstream of it.
candidate_sites: logos-protocol/cpp/implementations/plain/qvariant_rpc_value.cpp:23 — fromJsonValue() reads through QJsonValue, whose numbers ARE doubles
xfail.fix_is: a wire-representation change (an unsigned alternative in RpcValue, and not routing through QJsonValue); it touches every module, so it is deliberately not a drive-by fix

also.note: the C++ provider passes this one — its typed decode masks the loss

xfail.summary: `void` returns diverge: C++ answers JSON true, Rust fails the call
note: Pinned as a per-provider expectation in cases.json rather than hidden, so
the divergence is visible in the report. A consumer bound to the shared
`full_api` interface gets a different answer depending on which provider
it resolved to — which is exactly what a shared contract must not do.
Related: `void` is not a LIDL builtin, so it parses as Named("void") —
the same trap that made the Rust generator emit `-> Void` (fixed in
logos-rust-sdk e1e5350).
Not an xfail: the divergence is pinned as `expect_by_provider` in cases.json, which is where a KNOWN difference belongs. Listing it here too would report a passing cell as xpass.
xfail.fix_is: agree one answer for a void return across both provider backends

xfail.summary: a user map with a single `_bytes` key is reinterpreted as a byte string

measured.echoAny({\"_bytes\": \"aGk\"}): b'hi' on both providers — the map is gone

note: The canonical tagged-bytes form is structurally indistinguishable from
ordinary user data. Reachable from any `any` / `{tstr:any}` slot, i.e.
from anything a user can put in a map.
xfail.fix_is: out of scope here — it is a wire-format question (a reserved key needs to be unforgeable, or tagging needs to be out-of-band)

xfail.summary: the deferred-call sentinel key hijacks a call when it appears in user data
note: Same class as M3 but with a worse outcome: instead of a value being
reinterpreted, the call fails. The sentinel is checked with `contains()`
and no size guard, so any user map carrying that key is treated as a
pending-call marker.

xfail.summary: M1 seen through a typed [uint]: only the Rust provider reports it
note: Split from M1 because the C++ provider passes this exact cell — its typed decode coerces the degraded double back to uint64_t, hiding the loss the untyped cells expose.

xfail.summary: a bstr is UTF-8 mangled as soon as it is nested inside a container

measured.echoBytes(b'\\x00\\x80\\xff'): b'\x00\x80\xff' — exact as a top-level scalar, on both providers
measured.echoMap({k: <tagged>}): {'k': '\x00\ufffd\ufffd'} — a STRING, each byte >= 0x80 replaced by U+FFFD

note: This is the exact defect the canonical {"_bytes": ...} tag was introduced to
prevent (logos-protocol #21/#23), still reachable one level down.
The corruption is INBOUND, before the module: the Rust ext provider's
echoBlob decodes a record's bstr field into Vec<u8> and re-encodes it with
the same tagged encoder the scalar path uses, and it returned SIX bytes
(0x00 EF BF BD EF BF BD) for a three-byte input — i.e. it faithfully
re-tagged an already-replaced value. So neither the module nor its return
path is where the bytes are lost.
Same family as M1: a value nested in an untyped container goes through a
representation that cannot hold it. The typed top-level slots survive
because the typed decode never takes that path.
xfail.fix_is: not attempted here — like M1 it is a wire-representation question, and guessing the hop without proving it would be worse than recording the measurement

skip.note: JavaScript has no byte-string literal; the QML bridge excludes bstr by design
